Event Bus (Custom Devtools API)

The Event Bus provides a development-only pipeline event stream that can be used to build custom DevTools, diagnostic tooling, and runtime analytics for execution.

The Event Bus exposes pipeline events emitted during Vault execution through a shared observable interface. Subscribers can listen to these events and build custom recording, inspection, debugging, or visualization tools without altering pipeline behavior.

Event emission is gated by development mode. In normal usage, the Event Bus is intended for internal diagnostics, custom DevTools integrations, and analytics workflows during development.

Overview

The Event Bus is a singleton runtime channel for observing pipeline events emitted during Vault execution. It provides a single shared stream that development tools can subscribe to in order to inspect runtime activity.

Pipeline events are emitted as EventShape instances. These events may be consumed directly or enriched by custom tooling before being recorded, displayed, or analyzed.

The Event Bus is designed for observation only. It does not mutate state, control pipeline execution, or alter FeatureCell behavior.

Note

The Event Bus intentionally allows developers to emit custom events into the pipeline stream. This flexibility enables advanced diagnostics, analytics, and custom DevTools integrations. Because these events may be synthetic, developers should avoid emitting events that could interfere with or misrepresent actual Vault pipeline behavior.

In practice, pipeline events emitted by the Vault runtime represent authoritative execution signals, while custom tooling may optionally emit additional diagnostic events for debugging or instrumentation purposes.

Development Mode Scope

Event Bus emission is active only when development mode is enabled. This ensures that pipeline telemetry is available for diagnostics during development without becoming part of normal production execution behavior.

When development mode is inactive, pipeline events are not emitted through the Event Bus. Consumers may still obtain the singleton instance, but no pipeline event stream will be produced. 

{{`// app.config.ts
export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ 
      devMode: true,
    })
  ]
};`}}
 
{{`Vault({
  devMode: true,
});`}}
 
{{`// main.ts
Vault({
  devMode: true,
});`}}
API Surface

The Event Bus exposes a small API surface centered on a singleton access function, event emission, and pipeline observation.

Event Bus API
API Description

EventBus()

returns: EventBusContract

 Returns the shared Event Bus singleton used for pipeline event dispatch and observation throughout the application lifecycle.

nextPipeline(event)

input: EventShape

 Emits a pipeline event to subscribed observers when development mode is active.

pipeline$()

returns: Observable of EventShape

 Provides an observable stream of pipeline events for custom DevTools, diagnostics, and analytics subscribers.

The Event Bus instance is also exposed on the global window.sdux object for DevTools access during development.

Custom DevTools & Analytics

The Event Bus exists to support custom developer tooling built on top of pipeline telemetry. Subscribers may use the pipeline event stream to record execution history, enrich events with development-only metadata, or project pipeline behavior into custom diagnostics surfaces.

Typical development-only uses include:

  • Custom debugger panels
  • Execution trace recorders
  • Runtime analytics dashboards
  • Pipeline activity inspection tools
  • Extension-based DevTools integrations

Because the Event Bus exposes the raw pipeline stream, downstream tools are free to enrich, filter, aggregate, or redirect those events according to their own diagnostic needs.

Examples

One common usage pattern is subscribing to the Event Bus and recording pipeline events into a custom diagnostic history.

Example: Recording Pipeline Events
{{`import { EventBus } from '@sdux-vault/devtools';
import type { EventShape } from '@sdux-vault/shared';

const bus = EventBus();

const sub = bus.pipeline$().subscribe((event: EventShape) => {
  console.info('Pipeline event', event);
});

// later
sub.unsubscribe();`}}

Another common pattern is enriching pipeline events before storing them in a custom DevTools surface. This is how the built-in debugger records derived fields such as sequence ordering, timing metadata, event-loop heuristics, and latency categorization.

Example: Consuming the Event Bus in a DevTools Service 
{{`import { Injectable, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { EventBus } from '@sdux-vault/devtools';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class CustomDevtoolsService {
  private readonly bus = EventBus();

  pipeline$() {
    return this.bus.pipeline$();
  }
}`}}

The built-in debugger and DevTools UI both use the Event Bus as their pipeline telemetry source. This makes the Event Bus the primary integration surface for development-only tooling that needs to observe pipeline execution.
